column1: # The engine's --retier* startup rules as cases.  ONE file, TWO readers: tests/retier_rules_case_test.cpp runs the engine's own
# retier_parse_flag / retier_check / retier_check_helpers on each row; tests/install/test_retier_rules.py runs the installer's mirror
# (install/_retier_rules.py) on the same rows.  Both must give exactly the error text below ("-" = accepted).
# Columns, TAB separated:  name  helpers  args (space separated, flag order = engine order)  expected error
# Absent --adapt-every / --adapt-swaps mean the engine's defaults (4 and 96); the rows that pass them use 64 and 8.
# WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT SHOW: the C++ reader is a fixture, not the engine.  It calls retier_parse_flag / retier_check /
# retier_check_helpers (the real code) but re-implements generate.cpp's parse loop around them: the "unknown argument: X" and
# "<flag> needs a value" texts and the adapt defaults (4, 96) are a COPY of generate.cpp, so a row on those compares the mirror to the copy.
# Arguments split on one space (no quoted spaces); the token '' is an empty argument.  Numbers assume the engine's Linux LP64 (long 64 bit).
# Not covered at all: real startup (--serve, the model's cell count vs the routing counts, a live helper tier, STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE).
